newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean prosecutors wait for Chun, Roh to act.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean prosecutors wait for Chun, Roh to act.

text.p: South Korean state prosecutors said on Monday they planned final appeals to the Supreme Court in the cases of 10 former aides of ex-presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, who are charged with mutiny and treason.
However, they were holding off on appeals action on Chun and Roh to see whether the one-time heads of state would meet Monday's deadline to appeal themselves.
One of the 10 former aides, Park Jun-byung, an ex-general, was acquitted of all charges and that verdict was upheld by an appeals court last Monday.

The other nine were jailed for between 3-1/2 years and eight years. Prosecutors said they did not plan a final appeal in the cases of four other former military officers jailed along with Chun and Roh.

Prosecutors will challenge the legal basis of the appeal's court ruling before the Supreme Court, which does not have the power to change the sentences but can judge their legality. Prosecutors had been seeking heavier sentences.
Yonhaps news agency on Monday quoted lawyers for Chun and Roh as indicating that their clients would not appeal in order to spare the nation further turmoil.
